sections.Science News:
#### GRB 261110A continued to fade, strengthening its optical-afterglow identification

SVOM/ECLAIRs triggered on **GRB 261110A at 11:50:00 UTC on 10 November 2026**. Follow-up reported after the previous edition confirms that the candidate at **RA 350.8530709°, Dec +33.0630451°** continued to fade. CrAO/ZTSh measured **R = 22.30 ± 0.10** at 6.12 h and **R = 22.80 ± 0.09** at 10.81 h after the trigger (Vega magnitudes); SVOM/COLIBRÍ then measured **r = 23.60 ± 0.19 AB** between 14.57 and 16.88 h. [GCN 46228](https://gcn.nasa.gov/circulars/46228), [GCN 46223](https://gcn.nasa.gov/circulars/46223).

MITSuME observations beginning 8.7 min after the trigger did not detect the source, with the deepest stacked limits **g′ > 20.2, Rc > 20.3 and Ic > 19.3 AB**. Those limits are shallower than the later detections and therefore do not contradict the afterglow interpretation. [GCN 46222](https://gcn.nasa.gov/circulars/46222). The positional agreement and multi-epoch fading now make this a well-supported optical afterglow, but no redshift or spectroscopic classification had been reported by the cutoff. Because the measurements use different filters and magnitude systems and are not corrected for Galactic extinction, they should not be combined into a precision decay slope without a consistent reanalysis.

#### Fermi/GBM detected the likely long GRB 261111A; no counterpart was reported

Fermi/GBM triggered on **GRB 261111A at 11:27:07 UTC on 11 November 2026** and classified it as a **likely long GRB**. The final real-time localization was **RA 56.9°, Dec +5.8°**, with a **2.0° statistical uncertainty**; the distributed HEALPix map includes the estimated systematic component. [GCN 46224](https://gcn.nasa.gov/circulars/46224). An independent BALROG fit gave **RA 54.1°, Dec +6.1°**, a **3.2° 1σ statistical radius**, and an estimated additional **1° systematic error**. [GCN 46225](https://gcn.nasa.gov/circulars/46225).

MASTER-SAAO began imaging about 6.7 h after the trigger and reported no new optical source, with individual/coadded limits reaching approximately **18.9 mag** over portions of the broad GBM region. [GCN 46229](https://gcn.nasa.gov/circulars/46229). This is a gamma-ray detection with a degree-scale localization, not a confirmed multiwavelength or multimessenger association; the optical non-detection is coverage- and depth-limited.

#### Einstein Probe found the uncatalogued X-ray transient EP261111a

Einstein Probe/WXT triggered on **EP261111a at 13:25:10 UTC on 11 November 2026**. The WXT position is **RA 43.118°, Dec +44.444°**, with a **3-arcmin radius at 90% confidence**, including statistical and systematic uncertainty. An automatic FXT follow-up found an uncatalogued X-ray source at **RA 43.1202°, Dec +44.4365°**, with a **20-arcsec 90% confidence radius**. [GCN 46226](https://gcn.nasa.gov/circulars/46226).

Xinglong began optical imaging 0.391 h after the trigger and found no candidate within the WXT region to **g > 20.955 AB at 5σ**. [GCN 46227](https://gcn.nasa.gov/circulars/46227). MASTER-SAAO observed roughly 7.1 h after trigger with shallower unfiltered limits of about 17.8 mag. [GCN 46230](https://gcn.nasa.gov/circulars/46230). No X-ray flux, temporal classification, optical counterpart or redshift was available at the cutoff, so EP261111a remains an unclassified X-ray transient; the optical limits do not establish the absence of a counterpart.

#### A host redshift narrows—but does not settle—the interpretation of EP261105a

An ePESSTO+ spectrum obtained with NTT/EFOSC2 beginning **06:51 UTC on 11 November 2026** measures **z = 0.0765 ± 0.0002** for the proposed host galaxy of EP261105a, from Hα, Hβ, [O II], [O III] and [N II] emission lines. In the cosmology adopted by the observers, this corresponds to a luminosity distance of **347 Mpc**. If the galaxy is the true host, the previously reported **R ≈ 24.3** counterpart at 18 h has **M_R ≈ −13.6** after Milky Way extinction correction. [GCN 46231](https://gcn.nasa.gov/circulars/46231).

That luminosity is at the faint end of kilonova models, but the existing optical data are also consistent with a power-law decay. The spectroscopy secures the galaxy redshift, not the transient association: a higher-redshift transient in chance projection remains possible. The report therefore does not constitute a kilonova identification.

#### ASKAP and Murriyang confirmed the new repeater FRB 20261031B

ASKAP/CRACO detected two bursts from **FRB 20261031B** at **10:56:18.023 and 12:00:29.265 UTC on 31 October 2026**, separated by about one hour. They had signal-to-noise ratios **14 and 11** at a central frequency of **943 MHz** and a common dispersion measure of **581.4 pc cm⁻³**. Voltage capture localized the source to sub-arcsecond precision at **RA 01:15:25.41(6), Dec −80:39:18.6(6)**. Murriyang/Parkes detected a third burst on **5 November at 10:07:46.714 UTC**, with **S/N = 61.4** and rotation measure **22.1 ± 0.1 rad m⁻²**, confirming continued repetition. The discovery was reported on **11 November at 19:14 UTC**. [ATel 18153](https://www.astronomerstelegram.org/?read=18153).

A putative host has **r = 23.2** and photometric redshift **z = 0.6 ± 0.1** (68% interval). If that identification and photometric redshift are confirmed, the source could be the highest-redshift known repeater. Both conditions remain provisional: spectroscopy and a quantified association probability are needed before treating the redshift or record claim as established.

#### EP trigger 01709322452 was classified as a stellar flare

Einstein Probe/WXT triggered at **00:17:37 UTC on 12 November 2026**. An initial MASTER follow-up began 397 s after the trigger and found no new optical source to approximately **19.0 mag**. [GCN 46232](https://gcn.nasa.gov/circulars/46232). The EP team subsequently associated the X-ray event with **PM J04414+1404**, classifying it as a likely stellar flare with estimated **0.5–4.0 keV flux ≈ 6 × 10⁻¹¹ erg s⁻¹ cm⁻²** and luminosity **≈ 1.1 × 10³¹ erg s⁻¹**. [GCN 46233](https://gcn.nasa.gov/circulars/46233). This revised classification removes the basis for treating the trigger as an unidentified extragalactic transient.
